html:
An Egyptian bank founded in 1920 by the economist Talaat Harb and partners, to put Egyptian savings into Egyptian owned industry. It is one of Egypt's largest banks today.

It was born in the mood of the 1919 revolution against British control. Foreign banks and companies ran Egypt's economy, and its wealth rested on raw cotton shipped to British mills. Talaat Harb argued that political independence meant little without economic independence.

The bank set up a group of companies under the Misr name. Among them:

  • a spinning and weaving company at Mahalla, which became one of the largest textile works in the Middle East;
  • Studio Misr, the film studio at the heart of Egypt's film industry;
  • Misr Airwork, the airline that became EgyptAir;
  • companies in shipping, insurance and printing.

Talaat Harb was forced out in 1939 after a crisis in the bank. In 1960 Nasser's government nationalised it with the rest of the banking sector.
sum: An Egyptian bank founded in 1920 by the economist Talaat Harb and partners, to put Egyptian savings into Egyptian owned industry. It is one of Egypt's largest banks today.
